item.title: github: SCIM user responses now include a profileUrl attribute
item.description:
GitHub SCIM user responses now include the RFC 7643 standard profileUrl attribute. It returns the absolute URL of the GitHub account linked to the external identity.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Passkey-themed social engineering leads to identity and cloud compromise
item.description:
Microsoft describes a threat campaign using passkey-themed social engineering to compromise identities and extend access into cloud services. The activity includes MFA persistence, Microsoft Graph reconnaissance, and access to SharePoint, OneDrive, and email data, with guidance on detection and mitigation.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Pod Certificates and Cluster Trust Bundles
item.description:
Kubernetes 1.37 graduates Pod Certificates and Cluster Trust Bundles to GA, adding built-in support for workload X.509 identity and trust bundle distribution. The feature uses Kubelet, PodCertificateRequest objects, and signer controllers to issue and rotate certificates for TLS/mTLS while keeping key material on the node filesystem.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: ai: Building Agents that Act on Your Behalf with Toolboxes in Foundry
item.description:
Toolboxes in Microsoft Foundry are presented as a way to let agents act on a user’s behalf while handling delegated identity across tools and services. The post highlights using a private Entra-protected MCP server alongside Microsoft’s managed Work IQ MCP server in the same agent flow.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: security: Least privilege for AI agents: Identity, access, and tool binding
item.description:
Microsoft Security published a post on applying least-privilege principles to AI agents, focusing on identity, access control, tool binding, and auditing as agents become more autonomous.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: June 2026
item.description:
Microsoft’s June 2026 security update post says the month’s changes focus on identity and multicloud foundations, data protection across locations, and securing developer workflows for AI-related work. The provided excerpt does not include product-level details or specific feature announcements.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
